utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will issue the ruling on the next batch of statements recorded under the provisions of Rule 92 bis. Further to the ruling of the Trial Chamber on 20th February, we have considered the statements submitted on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Miroslav Tadic and Mr. Simo Zaric. The Trial Chamber has taken into account the accused persons' right to call witnesses in support of their defence and the Prosecution's right to test such evidence. The Trial Chamber rules as follows: Regarding the Defence of Mr. Miroslav Tadic, the statement D114/3, by DW 3/3, which is under seal, is admitted into evidence. Paragraphs 26 and 28 are struck out. The remainder of the evidence is mostly cumulative and the witness will not be cross-examined. The statement D115/3 by Mirka Petkovic is admitted into evidence. However, paragraphs 24, 31, 32, the last sentence of paragraph 40, and the rest of paragraph 46 after the first sentence will be struck out. The witness will not be cross-examined. The statement D116/3 by Zeljko Volasevic is admitted into evidence. However, paragraph 7 and the last sentences of paragraphs 8 and 10 are struck out. This witness will come for cross-examination for one and a half hours. The statement of D117/3 by Stanko Bojic is admitted into evidence. However, paragraphs 11 and 12 are struck out. The last sentence of paragraph 10 is also struck out. The witness will give oral evidence on matters contained in those paragraphs that are struck out, and one hour is allowed for the oral evidence. Cross-examination is also allowed and limited to one hour. The statement D118/3 by Hasan Pistoljevic is admitted into evidence. Paragraphs 17 and 18 are struck out. Oral evidence is allowed for those -- for the contents of those paragraphs, for one hour, and cross-examination is allowed for half an hour. The statement D119/3, by Djordje Dujkovic is admitted into evidence as character evidence only. Paragraphs 3 to 14 inclusive are struck out, as they discuss matters other than character. This witness will not be cross-examined. The statement D120/3 by Ilija Mihajle is admitted into evidence. However, paragraphs 14 to 18 inclusive are struck out. Oral evidence is allowed, for one hour, and cross-examination is also allowed, for one hour. The statement D121/3 by Marko Kuresevic is admitted into evidence. The Prosecution is allowed to cross-examination for one hour. The statement D122/3 by Muhamed Atic, a character witness, is admitted into evidence. Paragraph 6 and 7, which discuss other matters, are struck out. The statement D123/3 by Abdulah Aslanovic, a character witness, is admitted into evidence. No cross-examination. On statements submitted on behalf of Mr. Simo Zaric, the statement D33/4 by Djuro Progomet is admitted into evidence. Paragraphs 13, 15, 16, and 17 are struck out. There shall be no cross-examination. The statement D34/4 by Fadil Topcagic is admitted into evidence. However, paragraphs 41, 42, 46, 49, 57, 58, and 68, in addition to that, in paragraph 39, the last sentence, starting from "inside" up to "Crkvina" are struck off. Paragraph 61 is admitted only up to the words "measures about this crime." The rest of that paragraph is struck out. The witness will give oral evidence on matters contained in those paragraphs that are struck out, and oral evidence will be allowed for two hours. Cross-examination is allowed for two and a half hours. The statement D35/4 by Petar Karlovic is admitted into evidence. However, paragraphs 33 and 34 are struck out. Cross-examination by the Prosecution is allowed and restricted to the events of the 16th up to the end of the 17th of April, 1992, and cross-examination will be allowed for one hour. The statement D36/4 by Fatima Zaric is admitted into evidence only partially. The last paragraph -- the last part of paragraph 19, starting with the words "about 20 minutes" up to the end, and paragraphs 20 to 25, paragraphs 27, 28, and 30, are struck out. These paragraphs discuss the whereabouts and activities of Simo Zaric. The witness will give oral testimony on the events from the 16th to the 20th of April, 1992, and one and a half hours is allowed for that. Cross-examination will be allowed for one hour. The statement D37/4 by Vaso Antic is admitted into evidence. Paragraphs 15, 19, 24, and 25 are struck out. The witness will give oral testimony on the events described in those paragraphs, and one hour is allowed for that. Cross-examination will be limited to one hour. The statement D38/4 by Focakovic Hasim, a character witness, is admitted into evidence. However, paragraphs 15, 16, and 19 which discuss matters other than character are struck off. The statement D39/4 by Mihajlo Topolovac, paragraphs 1 up to 24 inclusive and paragraphs 28, 35, 36, and 37 are admitted into evidence. The rest of the paragraphs are struck off. The witness will give oral evidence on those paragraphs, and one hour is allowed. Cross-examination is also allowed for one hour. The statement of -- the statement D40/4 by Viktorija Topcagic who is a character witness, is admitted into evidence. However, paragraph 20 is struck out. The rest of the statements yet to be submitted and those submitted yesterday will be discussed at a later stage. We will continue with our proceedings. Please call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning, and please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Lazarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. Can you just tell me if you can hear me well. And if you please approach the microphone so that it can catch what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning. I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Just so before we begin, can you just have a pause when I ask you a question before you answer so that we don't have an overlap. Just try and pay attention to that. Thank you. Now, for the record, can you tell us your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Vladimir Sarkanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me when you were born and where?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 22nd of October, 1941, in Gornji Gradar [as interpreted], municipality of Pelagicevo -- Donji Zabar, municipality of Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your profession is now?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: Where did you complete your primary and secondary school?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I went to -- I went to school in several places, but I completed in Brcko. That's where I also completed my grammar school, and then I went to pursue my studies in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me which university you went to in Zagreb, which faculty, and what degree do you have?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I went to the law school. I have a law degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is called the first degree. This is just for the purposes of the Trial Chamber, for the record.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you completed this first degree of the law school, where did you start working?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1966, in Zagreb, and I started to work later, after completion of my military service, in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just tell me: From what time do you live in Samac?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I've been living in Samac since 1969.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you in relation to your military service in the JNA: Can you tell me if you have served it, where did you serve, and when?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I served my military service in the JNA from September 1967 until September 1968, and the first six months of my military service I went to the reserve officer's school, and then for six months I was in an artillery unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following your military service, did you have a rank? Did you obtain a rank?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Following the completion of my military service, I was a member of the reserve force with the rank of second lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following that, through serving in the reserves and military exercises, did you obtain any higher rank than the second lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I obtained the rank of captain first class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you something in relation to the reserve officers' school. Before this Court, we spoke about it on several occasions, so I wanted to ask you about your experience in relation to personnel being sent to the reserve officers' school in terms of their ethnic background of those students who went to that school. Was there -- was any attention paid to the ethnic structure of the students who went to the reserve officers' school?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Military school for reserve officers, all students from all ethnic backgrounds of Yugoslavia went to that school at the time from Bosnia-Herzegovina, proportionally, according to the number of inhabitants in the municipality. In the same way, members and cadets were sent to the reserve officers' school. So there were Serbs, Croats, Muslims in the school, and even ethnic minorities at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me something else in relation to your general background: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have children, grandchildren?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I have two sons and one grandson.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're a Serb by ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you some questions in relation to your party membership. Were you a member of any party? If so, at what time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of the Communist Party of Yugoslavia until it fell apart practically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Following that, did you join another party, after the communist league of Yugoslavia ceased to exist?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not a member of any party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which party do you vote for now?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: For the pensioners' party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Did you pursue any activities through any hunting associations? Are you perhaps still a member of a hunters' association?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I am a member of a hunters' association, but I don't hunt very frequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, can we have the name of that hunters' association that you're a member of?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Samac Hunters' Association, Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me now: I'm interested in your professional career. You said that you started to work in 1969. Can you tell me: Where did you work, and what was your occupation during your career?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th of May, 1969, I started to work at the then secretariat for the interior in Bosanski Samac, at a post of criminal inspector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: Until when did you do this work?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I was there until I was retired, which was on the 30th of June, 1987.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can conclude that throughout your working career, you were a police inspector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, throughout your period of work as an inspector at the public security station in Samac, at any time during that period was Simo Zaric chief of that public security station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Simo Zaric was at one point chief of the secretariat of the interior, where I worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simo Zaric, was he superior? Was he your superior at the time or was it a slightly different situation in place?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: He was not a superior to me at the time. Simo Zaric was the chief of the municipal secretariat of the interior in Bosanski Samac, while I worked at the crime department, which, organisationally speaking, belonged to the inter-municipal secretariat of the interior of Doboj. It had a kind of branch office in Samac for doing any work connected to the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if I understand this correctly, without wishing to imply anything, you worked at the public security station in Bosanski Samac, but your responsibility -- you were responsible for the Doboj?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We only used the premises of the municipal secretariat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've just been informed that we have something that is not clear enough in the transcript. You were responsible not for the Doboj but instead of that, your superiors were in the detachment in Doboj, detachment of the interior in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I just said, is that correct? Can you confirm, Mr. Sarkanovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: My superiors were in Doboj, while the work that I carried out together with my colleagues, this was in the area of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever a member or did you work for the state security service? You spoke about public security. I'm now asking you about state security.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, throughout your work, 20 years in the police station in Bosanski Samac, can you tell me whether this station, while you were working there, while you were employed there, did it have a certain reputation at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: You could say that it did, because the detachment that I work for, the section I worked for, it had very good results, enviously good results.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just ask you a couple more questions in relation to some details related to you. Now, we're speaking about the period before the 17th of April, 1992. Did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: At that time, and today, I have two hunting rifles and one handgun, which I received when I retired, from my colleagues, from the service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1987, you went into retirement. How did you spend the time during your retirement until about April 1992? What did you do? What was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: When I retired in 1987, most of my time I spent at my weekend house at the village of Pelagicevo, about 30 kilometres from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I came to Samac at the end of the autumn. I would spend my winter in Samac, and then in the second half of the spring, depending on the weather, I would go back to my weekend cottage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will now ask you something in relation to the atmosphere and some events that occurred in the territory of the Bosanski Samac municipality, and in the wider area, at the end of 1991 and beginning of 1992. Did you perhaps notice something, some change that occurred in relation to what it was like before? Was there some deterioration in the relationship between people? Were there any incidents that happened, and so on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I already said that most of the year I spent at my weekend cottage during that autumn, that is, late autumn of 1991, when I arrived in Samac. It was during my very first outings in the town I realised that there was no directness between the people, and even cordiality between the people, when I met the locals, when it was compared to the other times when I came to Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we answer one thing --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: That could be observed was a kind of fear and anxiety, a worry among the people which I explained through the proximity of the war in Croatia and the anxiousness that this war would be transferred to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come back to certain events later, but now I'd like to open another subject with you, and perhaps we can talk about it. And the subject is the 4th Detachment. First of all, can you tell me: Were you a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: In what way and when did you become a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I became a member of the 4th Detachment at the beginning of January 1992, in such a way that I responded to mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: In the 4th Detachment, did you have a post, a position?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were just a simple soldier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had the rank of a captain in reserve and you were still a simple soldier in the 4th Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was established as an infantry unit, and because I'm an artilleryman myself, at that time the 4th Detachment did not have any artillery, so I couldn't have had, strictly speaking, any command position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you tell me, then: When you became a member of the 4th Detachment, were you issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I received an automatic rifle of the Kalashnikov type, with one combat set of ammunition; and as far as the uniform is concerned, I was issued a winter jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now when we're speaking about the 4th Detachment, can you tell me: What was the ethnic structure of the members of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was heterogeneous. It consisted of all the different ethnic groups living in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among the commanders and other leading or commanding structures in the detachment, were there representatives of all the different ethnic backgrounds? I mean company commanders and such.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From the detachment commander level downwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other members of the detachment also issued weapons, like you were?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: All of them were given weapons, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This had nothing to do with their ethnic background, did it? Whoever was a member of the detachment would be given weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Regardless of their ethnic background, all of the members, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me: Who was the commander of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Radovan Antic was the commander of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the deputy commander? Just the name.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Jovo Savic was the deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the position of Simo Zaric there in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: He was the deputy commander for intelligence, morale, and security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Miroslav Tadic? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: He was deputy -- assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the headquarters of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The headquarters was on the premises of the Sit work organisation, the Mladost association of labour in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know where the AS cafe is. Can you tell me, in relation to that cafe, where is that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Just across the way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me now: Were any symbols displayed prominently on the command building, or anywhere in the vicinity, any symbols indicating that there was a military presence there or the headquarters of a military unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. There were the flags, the Yugoslav flag and the Bosnia-Herzegovina flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the 4th Detachment, let us elaborate, please. Was it part of a larger military formation? If so, who was at its head, and where was its headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment was part of the 17th Tactical Group, commanded by Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where the 17th Tactical Group was based, where was its command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The command or the headquarters was in the village of Pelagicevo, which is about 30 kilometres from Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this is not Samac municipality, is it; it's a different municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: That's the area of Gradacac municipality, or rather, was at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Throughout that period while you were a member of the 4th Detachment, as you said, since January 1992, were you physically present in a barracks or anything of that sort, or was life organised in a different way?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: There was no such thing as a barracks. Each member of the detachment lived in their own respective homes, and that was also where they kept their weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think there's no need for us to dwell on this any longer. Can we please move on to certain meetings which were held in connection with organising the 4th Detachment and with the aim of informing the public about the tasks of the 4th Detachment. Did you attend any such meetings? If so, please tell us when.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: At first, the establishment of the detachment caused certain dissent to arise among the population of Samac. A meeting was held at the memorial centre in Bosanski Samac at which the role and the reason for the establishment of the 4th Detachment were explained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were only members of the detachment present at that meeting, or was that a meeting of a broader nature, where other people attended too, meaning civilians also who were not members of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting was organised first and foremost for the benefit of the citizens who were not members of the detachment. There was a need to explain to them why the 4th Detachment had been established and what the reason was for its existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what the reason was for the setting up of the 4th Detachment? How was that presented to the citizens at the meeting? What exactly were they told? What were you told, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The reason that the 4th Detachment was set up was, first and foremost, the need to prevent interethnic strife, to prevent war from spilling over from the neighbouring Croatia into Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who spoke at that meeting, specifically?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Detachment commander and his assistant for morale were speaking at that meeting. His assistant for morale, intelligence, and security; specifically, Radovan Antic and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now, please, go back to the overall situation in the municipality and to certain events occurring at the time. Were you familiar with certain acts of sabotage, buildings being blown up throughout that period? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: As I've said, I did notice that the atmosphere was different when I came to Samac. As time went by, the situation kept deteriorating. There were acts of sabotage. Telegraph and electricity poles were being pulled down, news agents were being broken into. Hasan Ceribasic's holiday cottage had been broken into. The chapel at the Serbian cemetery was destroyed. There was an attempt to blow up the bridge over the River Sava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've spoken about these incidents, and I do not wish to dwell on this for too long, with the exception of one particular incident. Did you have any knowledge or information as to whether the police of Bosanski Samac had actually managed to track down any of the perpetrators of these acts of sabotage?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: After the national parties came to power, and after people were appointed to the leading positions at the SUP in Bosanski Samac along party lines, there were immediately divisions along party lines and along the ethnic lines, so that the work of that service at that time was not even felt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have information whether any of the perpetrators were actually found out?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I think not a single one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a person who has spent his whole life as a police inspector, his whole career, what would you say: What was the effect of that situation on the general sense of security among the citizens in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The effect was certainly very detrimental. Things kept happening. No perpetrators were ever found. This caused much discontent among the people and much apprehension as to what was potentially about to happen. Even more so when, on two occasions, even worse things happened. Citizens of Samac were wounded or even killed. On one occasion, two young men were killed at a cafe. On another, members of the reserve police force used firearms, wounding three members of the 4th Detachment in the process.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly let us speak about this incident where two young men were killed at the Valentino Cafe. First of all, let me ask you: What was your relationship to Kemal Bobic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Very good, even friendly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's beyond dispute that his son was one of the persons who were killed in that incident at the Valentino Cafe, and I think no one contested the fact that this happened because those young men were playing with a hand grenade. What I really want to know is what happened after that. Citizens gathered outside the police station. Were you around at that time? Were you present there? And what exactly did you notice?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there. That evening, I was in my flat, when, around 9.00 in the evening, my son came. He was aged about 15 at that time. And he told me that in one of the cafes, a grenade had exploded, wounding, as he told me, a number of young men. I put on my clothes quickly and I went to the centre. You could feel a sense of unease in the centre. There was a lot of disquiet. And I noticed that some of the citizens were walking towards the municipality building and the SUP building. Some of them told me that a rally was expected outside the SUP building in relation to these events. I was interested in this, and I came along. And outside the SUP building, I found Mr. Simo Zaric and Mr. Mihajlo Topolovac. There were about a hundred people there already, citizens mostly of Muslim ethnicity, among whom there were some people who blamed the event on Serbs and on Serbo Chetniks, as they called them. Among that group, I think a man named Jasarevic was particularly prominent. His nickname was Roma. This went on for a while, until at one moment Hadzialijagic spoke to the assembled citizens. Safet Hadzialijagic, called Coner. He appealed to those gathered there to go home, to disperse, and allow the SUP some time to clarify the situation. Once people started to disperse, I suggested to Mr. Zaric and Mr. Topolovac, since I had in the meantime been told that one of those two young men who had been killed was the son of Kemal Bobic, I suggested that we go to Kemal's house to express our condolence. We did eventually go to Kemal Bobic's house, and outside the house we found a small group of people. We commiserated to Kemal and his wife. I asked Kemal whether he needed anything with regard to the burial of his son. He asked me whether I could lend him a certain amount of money. I promised to do so. And the next day I sent the money to him with my younger son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the specific amount of money, and did Kemal Bobic give this money back to you? Did he pay you back at any time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: This was a thousand German marks, and Kemal immediately returned the money to me after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I plan on returning to Kemal Bobic at a later stage, but now tell me about another incident which you have also referred to, namely, the wounding of three members of the 4th Detachment. What do you know about that particular incident? What was it that actually happened there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: That evening, a patrol of the reserve police force, for reasons I did not know, opened fire on a moving vehicle, a vehicle carrying three members of the 4th Detachment. All three of them were wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember who these members of the reserve police force were who opened fire on members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I think Mersad Mesic perhaps -- I know that he was a butcher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My objection is to, I think -- perhaps it could be clarified whether the witness was actually there and saw this or whether it's something he actually heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, I don't think the witness was actually answering my question, because he was answering about who the wounded were and not who actually should -- but I will clarify this. I have no problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When this incident happened, were you present at the scene?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your information about this event is hearsay really?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's hearsay. I can only tell you what I've heard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If that's not a problem, could you please tell us what you heard about it. First of all, who were the men who had opened fire on members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Two reserve police officers: Izetbegovic, I know he was Izo's son, but I don't know his first name. And the other man's last name was Srna and his father was a railway worker. Those were younger people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We do not intend to dwell on this now. Just tell me, please, if you can remember the names of the people who were wounded, the three members of the 4th Detachment. You started telling us. There was an objection by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, one of them was called Mirsad Mesic. Another's name was Ramusovic, nicknamed Tota. I'm not sure about his first name. And the third one was Danilo Vitomir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. At that time - and we have already heard this from a number of witnesses' testimonies - there were some rallies, citizens' rallies, in the area of the Bosanski Samac municipality, or rather, in the town of Bosanski Samac itself. Did you attend any of these rallies? We used to refer to them as peace rallies here. Did you attend any of these rallies; and if so, can you please tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were a number of those, and I attended one which was held at the local cinema in Samac. The speakers at that meeting, I think there was Sulejman Tihic, nicknamed Mane, and Simo Zaric. The message at those rallies, as a rule, was the need to prevent interethnic strife and the need for coexistence, peaceful coexistence, as well as the need to prevent war from spilling over from Croatia into Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I withdraw this question. Can you please tell me: The 16th of April, 1992, where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: In Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your family with you on the 16th of April in Samac?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: My wife and my younger son. The elder son was already in Italy. He was abroad. His girlfriend lived there, and eventually he stayed there. They got married. He lives there now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about the day of the 16th of April of 1992. Did anything special happen on that day? Did you notice anything out of the ordinary?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Personally, I didn't. A day like any other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's talk about the evening of the same day. What happened in the evening? Can you tell us, please: Where were you? What happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992, I was at home in my flat. Suddenly, my wife shook me awake at about 3.00 in the morning, or perhaps a little later, on the 17th of April, telling me that she had heard sounds of shooting and an explosion in the town. I didn't pay much attention to that, because sounds of shooting were not completely unusual. This had happened before. And yet, I rang up the police station, the SUP, to see if anything was happening. The phone lines were down, so this was not a good way for me to obtain any information. I tried to call the duty officer of the 4th Detachment, but the same thing happened, because the phone lines were down, so I couldn't get through to them. In the meantime, though, I heard some clamour in the corridor of my building, the building where I live. I came out into the corridor. I saw two of the residents, who also worked for the police, and they were asking themselves the same question: What was happening? After a while, and after commenting an exchanging opinions on what it might have been, we all went back to our flats and back to sleep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please just tell us the names of those two gentlemen, the neighbours whom you found in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Savo Savic and Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you went back to sleep, were there still sounds of shooting to be heard?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: As we were still in the corridor, the shooting had stopped, so I went back to my flat -- I went back to sleep, I woke up the same day about 7.00 or 8.00 in the morning. And as I was sipping my morning coffee with my wife, the phone rang. I picked up the receiver and realised that it was the duty officer of the detachment, telling me to come to the detachment immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now we're speaking about the 17th of April, in the morning. You were called by the duty officer from the detachment and told you to come to the detachment. Did he tell you what was the reason for that and what was happening?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: He told me that during that night -- in fact, I had asked him what was happening that night and why was there shooting, and he then told me that specials from Serbia, as he called it, and the Serbian police, had taken over the control over the key facilities in Samac, and that that was the reason why I had to report to my unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lazarevic. I wonder, Mr. Sarkanovic, just to clarify: You had said that on the morning of 17th of April, 1992, at approximately 3.00 a.m., you tried to make some phone calls and the phones weren't working. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And then approximately five hours later, at 8.00, you got up, you were having your coffee, and then you received a phone call, so at that point in time, obviously the phones were reconnected. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The call was about 9.00 in the morning on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the duty officer called you. Can you tell us: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I got ready, and while I was getting ready, through the window of my apartment, which is located in the central part of Samac, I saw, on the plateau in front of the department store, and in the part of the market which is closer to my apartment, I saw a group of armed civilians, among whom I recognised my neighbours, the Atic brothers, the Sabanovic neighbour, Ekac, Bicic brothers. They were armed with firearms. And considering that one of them I had filed charges against because of rape, I decided that if I went out of the apartment, this could lead to some unfortunate things happening. So I called the duty officer at the detachment. I explained to him what the situation was and I asked for permission to arrive at the detachment once the conditions are right, and he gave me the permission. So I did not go to the detachment on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let us just analyse something you have said in relation to your answer. When you said "Ekac," can we please be precise about who that was?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: That was Esad Dagovic, also known as Ekac. He was a waiter at the pizzeria run by Bicic brothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you also tell me: You mentioned that you had arrested one of these persons because of rape. Among those you've mentioned, who is that person?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: That's Kemal Atic, also known as Kilo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to the last answer. I'm sorry. I was a little bit late in responding, Your Honours. The evidence in relation to rape, I'd ask that that be struck from the record. It's not relevant to these proceedings and it wasn't put to the witnesses when they gave evidence. There's certainly no evidence of any conviction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. He simply said that he had arrested him for these charges; that's all. It wasn't a conviction. The witness said he had arrested this person on charges of rape; that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I may give the answer to what my colleague has just stated. First of all, one of these -- none of these persons -- these persons that was mentioned was not a witness here, was not -- has nothing to do with the proceedings here. This raping happened before the war started and it had nothing to do with the proceedings. But it just explains why this witness didn't feel safe of walking outside when he saw this person armed with Kalashnikov. So I don't really see what is the basis for the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, there is no basis, actually. You can go ahead, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So, sir, you told us who you saw. Now, to just clarify things fully: All of these persons that you then saw, can you tell us what is their ethnicity, Atic, Dagovic, Bicic brothers?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: They're all Muslims, of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you thought it was not safe, and you said that you stayed at home. On that day, did you go out at all, or was there anything else that was happening outside? Were there people coming or going?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Throughout that day, 17th of April, I did not leave my apartment, because through the window of the apartment, I was able to see that group -- which occasionally would split into smaller groups and then they would get together again. Throughout the day they were on the plateau in front of the department store and the part of the market which borders with the plateau in front of the department store.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were watching that through the window of your apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, through the window. I already said that the apartment is located in the central part of Samac. So through the window, I have a view, in fact, an overview of the south and the western part of that part of town, considering that most of these walls are glass walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That night of the 17th, did you spend it at home?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The night of the 17th to the 18th I spent in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So now we're talking about the 18th of April. Can you tell me: What is happening on the 18th of April, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, in the morning, immediately after I got up, I looked through the window and I saw a small group of people that I couldn't, in fact, recognise, because they were a little further inside the market area. And at about 1000 hours, somebody knocked on the door of my apartment, and I opened the door. I saw three unknown people in front. They were dressed in camouflage uniforms. Their faces were painted with black paint. These people asked me if I had a weapon. I told them that I had an automatic rifle which had been issued in the detachment to me, and that I had a certificate to prove it, and that I had my personal weapons, two hunting rifles and a handgun. I showed them the permits. After that, they went further into the building, which means that they went upstairs, towards the higher floors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You already said that these people were unknown to you, that you didn't recognise them. Did they perhaps have a characteristic accent that could give you some indication as to where these people came from?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: It could be observed that these people were from Serbia, because they used the Ekavica dialect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they go from apartment to apartment, as far as you were able to observe, of course?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw them for the first time when they came to my door, in front of my apartment. But where they went, I can assume that they went to the apartments that were behind mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not observe any further?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course not. As soon as they told me that I was all right, I closed the door and went back to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Somewhat later, was there anything else that was happening in the street that you were able to observe after that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Soon afterwards, I first heard and then I saw a vehicle, a moving vehicle, from which someone was using a loudspeaker to call on to the citizens to hand over the weapons that they had, the weapons that they had without a permit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move to the afternoon of the 18th of April. Did you go to report to the detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: In the afternoon hours, about 1700 hours, when I realised, when I was absolutely certain that on the plateau in front of the department store there was no one to be seen, then I took the automatic rifle and I went to the command of the 4th Detachment, which in the meantime changed location, and it was in a private house now, also in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where approximately, where was that house when you reported? Where was the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The house was in the 4th District, which is located near the defence dam by the Bosna River, and it is owned by Jovo Dusanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came to the command, who did you find there? What were you told?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: At the command, I saw the detachment commander, Mr. Antic. I saw Simo Zaric and some others, some soldiers. And the duty officer of the detachment, I think, was second lieutenant Nikolic. I don't know. I know his father's name is Vojko. I'm not sure about his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, that Nikolic is not --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Not Lieutenant Colonel. This is a local from Samac. His father's name is Vojko. I don't know what the son's name is. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What were you told?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: He told me to report to my company commander and that I could find him at one part of the dam, as I said, which goes along the right bank of the Bosna River. And it goes towards the village of Prud. That is on the western part of Samac, towards the village of Prud.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. Not dam, but embankment.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I went there and I found Celikovic, Milan, who was the commanding officer, and he told me to which of the positions of that embankment I should go.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at your combat position at the embankment, on the embankment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I stayed on the embankment the night between the 18th and 19th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. During that time while you were on the embankment, were there any hostilities? Was there any opening of fire?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: There was sporadic fire from the direction of Prud.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You already said that you only spent that night on the embankment. What happened on the 19th of April, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of April, in the morning -- on the 19th of April --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: -- a courier came from the command and told me that I had to report to the security station in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just to make it clear for the transcript: That was 19th of April, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was 19th, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the police station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I immediately went to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: The situation that you found at the very entrance to the police station, what's happening there? What did it look like?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in front of the building where the police station was, I found an unusual crowd of people. There were persons there who were in the reserve force of the police, in the active force of the police. There were civilians, there were people who were in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go inside? And if you did, what did you see inside?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I went inside, because that's why I came for. And in front of the duty officer's office, so in front of that duty officer's office, the office where the duty officer sits, I was met by the then unknown person who was dressed in a black uniform or a suit - I cannot tell you what that was, because it was of a very unusual type and colour - he handed me his -- he put his hand out and, by calling me by my name, he congratulated me on the Serbian Republic. I shook his hand. We kissed. And while that was happening, out of the corner of my eye, I saw the commander of the police station, to whom I immediately afterwards I received the congratulations. I went to see him and went to ask him who that person was. Savo Cancarevic replied that this was Stevan Todorovic, that he was now the chief of the public security station. I told Savo that I was called to the SUP, to which he answered that I had to report to Milos Savic, who was already at the SUP and in the former premises of the crime department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is usually time for a break, I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, and we'll continue at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sarkanovic, you probably remember where we left off before the break. You said that you had seen a man wearing black uniform, a man you had not known before. He congratulated you on the Serb Republic. And then you left with Savo Cancarevic, who told you that that man was Stevan Todorovic and that you should go and see Milos Savic at the crime department. So you went to see Milos Savic. First of all, tell me: Milos Savic's office, the office that Milos Savic was using, was that on the ground floor or on one of the upper floors of the police station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The crime department is on the first floor of the secretariat building, in the left-hand half of the building, as you climb the main staircase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find Milos Savic in those offices? If so, please tell us what happened: What you told him and what he told you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I found Milos Savic in an office that I used to work in. We greeted each other, and Milos said that pursuant to an order of the secretariat for military affairs, I was to be transferred to the crime department and that my task would be crime prevention and finding out the perpetrators. He also told me that at the station there were a number of persons in detention who were to be interviewed with regard to the circumstances of their arming themselves or their belonging to paramilitary units. Furthermore, he showed me two documents, which I later used when I interviewed the prisoners. One of them was a list of a self-organised citizens of Samac for the defence of the town, and the other document was a mobilisation chart and an organisation chart for the units organised by the Party of Democratic Action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just hold on, please, for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Document D14/4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sarkanovic, we are lucky to have the original of the document here tendered into evidence. Can you please look at it carefully.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: This is one of the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please place it on that thing next to you, the ELMO. This is one of the documents Milos Savic showed you on the 19th. Did he perhaps tell you where the document came from, where it had been found, and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Milos told me that the documents had been found in the cupboard, or rather, in the desk of the commander of the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of this commander of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. I may be able to remember in the further course of my testimony, but right now I just can't seem to remember the name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But you are certain that this is the same document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... document any more. The next one would be D25/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In respect of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first three pages of these documents are marked as ID, and the rest of the document is admitted into evidence as full exhibit. So I would like the witness to see the whole document, so first three pages which are marked as ID, as well as the other pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There are these three pages missing here in this copy. Place on the ELMO, please, for the benefit of our clients.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, can you please have a look. The first three pages, as well as the remaining pages of this document. You can look at it while it's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I've looked at it. If I may just answer your previous question. I've just remembered the name of the commander of the reserve police force. The name is Namko [as interpreted] Suljic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this. You've looked through this document. Is this the same document that, on the 19th of April, 1992, when you came to the police station, Milos Savic showed you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this document used or actually shown to persons from whom you were taking statements?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Every single individual that I interviewed, I showed the list. That's in case the person's name was actually on the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just another question in relation to this. You have now looked through this document. Have there been any changes or amendments or additions to this document, as far as you can tell, additional words being typed in?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can please tell us, because on the transcript the name is misspelt. What's the name -- the first name of Suljic, the commander of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Namik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... D26/4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you managed to look through this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this document used too? Was this another document that Milos Savic showed you on the 19th of April?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use this document during interviews? Did you show this document to persons from whom you were taking statements?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: As I've said, both documents were shown to persons whom I interviewed, if their name was on the list, or in the documents, rather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, you had these documents very often in your hands. Have there been any changes or amendments, so to speak, to these present copies of these documents?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I had copies of these documents with me on a daily basis. I can't notice any changes or additions or amendments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You are now at the police station, and Milos Savic tells you what your tasks are. He shows you these documents. Tell me: Did you conduct interviews with the persons detained there? Just tell me yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll go back to this. This is crucial in terms of the indictment. But first of all, I want to ask you about Mr. Zaric and his presence at the police station. In relation to the 19th, when you arrived, when did you first see Mr. Zaric?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: At the police station, I first laid eyes on Mr. Zaric the next day, on the 20th of April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But let us try to focus your testimony on a number of issues that are interesting for us, the Defence of Mr. Zaric. I will ask you a number of brief questions in connection with Mr. Zaric. It is clear that you two had met before. Tell me now: When you saw Mr. Zaric for the first time there, was he wearing a uniform, and what kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was wearing a uniform. This was an olive-drab uniform, olive-drab, the kind used by soldiers in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. During those first days, was Mr. Zaric wearing the same uniform during those first days since the 19th or, rather, the 20th?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 20th he was wearing the same uniform; that's for sure. The next time I saw him, I'm not sure if he was wearing olive-drab or the camouflage uniform. It was several sizes too large and he tried to make it fit. Certain jokes were cracked about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That was a military uniform - let us just make this clear - not a police uniform?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was a military uniform, olive-drab, the kind of uniform used or, rather, worn by soldiers of the then army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll go back to Mr. Zaric, but there's another thing I'd like to ask you now. You came back to town from those positions and you were in at the police station. Did you notice anything in connection with white armbands or people wearing white armbands; and if so, please tell us what you noticed exactly.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't go to town very often during those days, but yes, I could indeed notice that a number of citizens who were not members of the 4th Detachment were wearing white armbands. I think it was the upper right arm that they wore it on. But I know that persons whom I interviewed did not wear such white armbands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us try to elaborate, please. The soldiers of the 4th Detachment, they were wearing white armbands, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The soldiers of the 4th Detachment, yes, yes, they were wearing white armbands on their left shoulder strap. Depending on the occasion, the colour of the armband would be changed. At the beginning, white armbands were used, and later, the colour would change.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us leave these soldiers aside for the time being. Let's talk about persons who were not members of the 4th Detachment, civilians, so to speak. You said that you had noticed that some of them had been wearing white armbands too?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: As I've said, I did see civilians, that is, persons who were not members of the 4th Detachment, wearing white armbands, but those were usually worn on the upper right arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps know the reason why those civilians were wearing white armbands? Had there been an order or a decision binding them, indeed, to wear these white armbands?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear that there was any decision like that, or order, but maybe citizens simply identified with members of the 4th Detachment, because this soon ceased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object. Apart from the leading, it's purely speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness doesn't seem to know why those were wearing armbands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm aware --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: White armbands.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- I will rephrase in another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, just another question related to the white armbands. Those persons whom you saw wearing white armbands - and I am talking about civilian now - those persons, were they from one particular ethnic group or were persons of all the different ethnic groups wearing those?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: All the different ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More specifically, please: Have you seen any Serb civilians wearing white armbands?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: At the entrance to my building, the building where my flat is, outside the entrance there's a family house where two elderly people, two elderly Serbs, live, Cvijeta and Milan Voskic [Realtime transcript read in error "Boskic"], going out or coming back into my building, I could notice that they too were wearing white armbands around their upper right arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please state again the last name of Cvijeta and Milan.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Voskic, Milan and his wife Cvijeta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us please go back to Mr. Zaric at the police station. Mr. Zaric, did he come up to you and Milos Savic? Did you talk about what he was doing there and how he came to be there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of April, 1992, Mr. Simo Zaric came to the SUP building, to the offices of the crime department, to the office in which I was staying, and Milos Savic too. After greeting us, he said that the commander sent him to look at the statements that we had taken from prisoners and see whether there was any information therein that could be useful to the army. And he also said that he would come back to do the same thing again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he on that occasion look at any of the statements which you had already taken?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Milos Savic and I had finished a number of interviews the day before, and we noted the circumstances surrounding the interviews. Milos Savic kept these statements and he gave them to Simo Zaric to look at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we just clarify one point in connection with that? Milos Savic, in relation to you, did he hold any particular position? Was he your superior in that section?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Milos Savic was the chief of the crime department. Even before these events, he had been an active member of the crime department.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from you and Milos Savic, was there anyone else working for the crime department? Was anyone else present at the crime department from the moment you joined?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: There was a crime technician there named Zoran Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. So that was the crime department, to all intents and purposes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the 20th of April now. Mr. Zaric is at the police station. You've already named Mr. Sulejman Tihic during your testimony. On the 20th of April, was an interview conducted with Mr. Tihic? How? Under what circumstances? Who was present? Who took the statement? What was the condition of Mr. Tihic on that day? Tell me that and any other details which you can recall in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: That morning when I came to the SUP building, Milos told me that he had been told by either the commander or the chief of SUP that on that day I would be conducting an interview with Sulejman Tihic, who was one of the detained citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment. Tell me: Did you know Sulejman Tihic from before, and what were your relationships with Tihic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I knew Sulejman Tihic practically from the moment I arrived in Samac, because it's a small place and everyone knows everyone else, particularly because Tihic at one point was a public prosecutor, and as somebody who was employed at the crime department, I was in close connection with Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your personal relationships with Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Good. Very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you found out that you had to conduct an interview with Mr. Tihic. Was he brought to the SUP? Was there anyone else present?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The usual practice was that citizens who were detained would be brought to us one by one. When Sulejman Tihic was brought to my office, I think that in the office next to me and Mr. Zaric there was also Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: What was the appearance of Mr. Tihic when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic was quite frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you? Who spoke to him? How did that proceed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: First we said hello to each other, and some informal talk. We started the interview. During that interview, he said that he had been detained in the police station, that the camouflaged policemen from Serbia had beaten him. It was possible to see on him the traces of the beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: Who took the statement from Sulejman Tihic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I just said: I started, and then Mr. Zaric said that he would want to speak with Sulejman Tihic to conduct the interview, and then I left the office to do something else, except that I would return to that office every now and then to see how Sulejman was, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether, by any chance, during the interviews while you were there, was there any talk of Sulejman Tihic being released?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: We encouraged Mr. Tihic. We told him that there was no reason for him to be further detained in the station after the interview. So in that sense, we told him that after the interview he would be released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you believe that, what you said to Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I believed that. I firmly believed that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This interview with Mr. Tihic went on for a while. Do you know what happened after that? Were you perhaps present when this interview was completed, when his statement was finished and signed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: By the end of the day, again I returned to the office where Simo Zaric was taking the statement from Sulejman Tihic, and then I was told - in fact, it was Simo who told me - that in the meantime he had spoken to the chief of the station, Stevan Todorovic, and that Stevan had a priori refused to release Sulejman Tihic to go home. Then I proposed that we should try and put Tihic in a premises designed for detention, where at the time there was no other detained citizen, in order to avoid the meeting between specials from Serbia and Tihic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your motive?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I just said: In some way to hide Sulejman Tihic from the specials, we placed him in the premises for detention where the specials didn't go to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you already said that you were not present during the entire interview, that is, during the entire statement-taking procedure from Tihic by Simo Zaric. But to the extent that you were present, were there any threats, any blows, any insults, anything that was possibly destined for Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. It was a correct attitude, even more than correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. A number of witnesses who testified here spoke about certain things that occurred at the time, and now I'd like you to tell us what you know about this. Were detained persons beaten?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not all of them, but most of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see? Where, when?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The office where I worked has a view of the yard of the TO building, where there were detained citizens. I had the opportunity to see that it was most frequently the specials from Serbia, and sometimes police members were beating the prisoners. There were also cases when prisoners were beating each other, most probably upon someone's instructions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see any other occurrences that should not have happened in a police station and certain acts that should not have occurred against detained persons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I already said: When a detainee is beaten, that is enough to say that this is improper behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: Were there any things that occurred when personal items were taken from the prisoners; and if so, can you tell us who?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you a specific example when this was done, but I know that there was talk of specials from Serbia brought prisoners and then released them, with the sole purpose of extracting money from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: To you, as a man who spent 20 years of active service in the police, what was your attitude towards such acts and such behaviour and occurrences that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course negative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me now: Did you ever go inside the TO building, you personally, during the time that prisoners were kept there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: Never. It was only once that I went into a room where prisoners were kept, and that was when -- because I wanted to see Kemal Bobic, aforementioned, about whom I had -- I heard that he had been imprisoned. And I asked the commander of the police station where Kemal was, and when he told me that Kemal was in the office in the lower part of the SUP building, in an office almost opposite the duty officer's room, I went to see him. On that occasion, apart from Kemal, I saw an office full of other citizens of Samac. I didn't spend a long time there. I gave some cigarettes to Kemal and I left. That was the only time that, apart from conducting interviews, individual interviews with detainees, that was the only time I had entered a detention room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: On that occasion when you entered that particular office, what can you tell us about the conditions of accommodation of these people there?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
utterances.text: The conditions were terrible. You can imagine when a room, say, that is 12 metres square large, more or less, that when there are 10 or 15 people in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to ask you some questions about specials from the police. We have started about this subject, and you said that they had beaten up prisoners. Can you tell me: How frequently did you see them at the police station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR SARKANOVIC
